summary: The candidate adds valid regression coverage for an existing hidden-state response offset fix, but does not reproduce or verify the original Kimi-K3 generated-reasoning leak. The proposed causal chronology is contradicted by repository history: upstream PR #30177 is already an ancestor of the official v0.5.17 tag that the reporter identified as affected.

tests.what_was_measured: Candidate regression suite: 9 tests and 2 subtests passed against the checked-out candidate source.
Independent GPU cases for FULL capture with a non-stored/non-requesting two-row request and LAST capture with mixed request modes; expected offsets and literal row values matched.
The merge of upstream PR #30177 predates and is contained in the official v0.5.17 tag, contradicting the candidate's stated release chronology.
sglang and batch_result_processor imported from /job/repo/python; PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 used the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X.

gpu_evidence: Independent tensor slicing checks executed on cuda:0, reported by ROCm as AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, and returned the expected FULL and LAST packed-row selections.
remaining_counterexamples: The reported reasoning leakage can occur for ordinary generation requests that do not request returned hidden states; the candidate test does not exercise that path.
The official v0.5.17 tag already contains the cited hidden-state offset correction, yet the original issue reports the symptom on v0.5.17.

No candidate test exercises Kimi-K3 generation, concurrent HTTP requests, tensor parallelism across eight B300 GPUs, or repeated randomized scheduling needed to seek the reported intermittent symptom.
remaining_limitations: The issue has no deterministic reproducer, so the original failure was not reproduced on the prepared base.
The reported architecture is eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs with CUDA 13.0; the review environment provides one AMD MI350X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2.
The GPU checks validate only hidden-state response offset accounting, not generated-text semantic isolation or the full serving path.
No native rebuild was needed because the candidate changes only Python tests and report files.
